fixes.explanation: True, friend. Luke 15:5 says that when he finds it, “…he joyfully puts it on his shoulders…” Joyfully, friend. The text says the man is happy about this.

Yes, friend. Luke 15:2 says the Pharisees and scribes began to grumble. Tax collectors and sinners were gathering around to listen to Jesus (Luke 15:1), and the grumbling started when they saw who was gathering. Jesus is about to answer them with a parable.

No soldiers in this scene, friend. Luke 15:1 mentions tax collectors and sinners gathering around to listen to Jesus, and then Luke 15:2 says the Pharisees and scribes began to grumble. The Romans never show up in these verses. The complaining comes from the Pharisees and scribes.

Not the complaint here, friend. In Luke 15:2 the grumbling is about who Jesus welcomes and who He eats with. Healing doesn't come up at all in this passage. The Pharisees and scribes say, “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”

Reasonable plan, friend, but that's not what Jesus says. He asks, “What man among you… does not leave the ninety-nine in the pasture and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it?” (Luke 15:4) The man goes after the one that is lost. I think the ninety-nine are in for a very quiet stretch.

No waiting around in this one, friend. Jesus says she does “…light a lamp, sweep her house, and search carefully until she finds it?” (Luke 15:8) She goes after that coin herself, and she searches until she finds it.
